blocks.text: World

British police said Tuesday that two men have been arrested over a suspected burglary at the Royal Family's Sandringham Estate. It follows reports that the home of Prince William and Princess Catherine on the vast royal estate was broken into on Monday.
Princess Catherine and William, son of King Charles, were not at the residence
British police said Tuesday that two men have been arrested over a suspected burglary at the Royal Family's Sandringham Estate.
It follows reports that the home of Prince William and Princess Catherine on the vast royal estate was broken into on Monday.

Norfolk Police said that officers were called Monday evening to reported "suspicious activity" at the address. After a search involving police dogs, drones and a helicopter, two men were arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespassing.

Anmer Hall, which has 10 bedrooms, was a wedding present to the couple from the late Queen Elizabeth II. William and Kate have used the house at Sandringham Estate in Norfolk, about 170 kilometres north of London, as a country residence on weekends and holidays.
The couple and their three children spend most of their time at Forest Lodge in Windsor, west of London, which they have described as their "forever home."
Previous security incidents
Intruders have breached royal properties several times over the years.

In October 2024, burglars broke into the Windsor Castle estate west of London and stole a pickup truck and a quad bike from a farm building. Charles and Queen Camilla weren't at Windsor Castle at the time.

Anmer Hall, a Georgian country house, is shown in 1973. Built in 1802, the property became part of the Royal Family's Sandringham Estate in 1898. (Leonard Burt/Central Press/Hulton Archive/Getty Image)

Three years earlier, a man armed with a crossbow was detained on the castle grounds. Jaswant Singh Chail was later sentenced to nine years in prison after admitting he had been encouraged by a chatbot to kill Queen Elizabeth.

In 1982, intruder Michael Fagan managed to sneak into the Queen's private chambers while she was in bed. Elizabeth spent 10 minutes chatting with the burglar before raising the alarm when he asked for a cigarette.

blocks.text: As well, there was a security incident earlier this year at Sandringham when the former Prince Andrew was allegedly threatened by a masked man while walking his dogs.

A court case for the 39-year-old man who was charged in connection with the incident is ongoing. Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, stripped of his royal titles and removed from his longtime Windsor Castle resident following damaging revelations regarding his relationship with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, now lives at Marsh Farms on the Sandringham estate.
Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham, left, greets Prince William ahead of their meeting at 10 Downing Street in London on Tuesday. (Toby Melville/Reuters)
The latest incident came as William visited Prime ‌Minister Andy Burnham at the British leader's office at 10 Downing Street.

While the British royals often mingle with political leaders and government ministers at formal occasions, visits to Downing Street, ​the official residence of British leaders since 1735, are more infrequent.
The pair were said to have met for about an hour, discussing issues like homelessness.
